chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Yafur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man drinks the fermented nabidh (drink), his testimony is not accepted in anything regarding drinks, even if he describes what you describe."

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A traditional fermented drink made from raisins or other fruits

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the testimony of someone who drinks fermented nabidh?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *'illat* (legal cause) linking the consumption of fermented nabidh to the invalidation of testimony (*shahadah*) specifically in matters concerning beverages. Scholars note that this restriction is not a general disqualification but a targeted one, ensuring that a witness's potential bias or lack of precision in the specific domain of their consumption does not compromise their credibility in that area.
